query: For a high-entropy alloy designed as a single-phase solid solution and exhibiting a favorable strength–ductility combination, what single testable hypothesis proposes an intervention to preserve toughness after thermal exposure and subsequent loading? Explain the hypothesized mechanism, predict the outcome relative to the same alloy tested under identical conditions without the intervention, define the applicable exposure and loading regime, identify supporting evidence from prior observations, and specify an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a controlled, low-volume fraction of a reticulated Laves phase via minor Cr addition to a single-phase BCC high-entropy alloy will preserve fracture toughness after thermal exposure at 1200–1400 °C and subsequent compressive loading, by arresting grain boundary decohesion and suppressing brittle intergranular fracture that typically follows phase decomposition.
generation.material_initial_state: Single-phase BCC solid solution high-entropy alloy (e.g., NbMoTaWV or CrMoNbWV type) with equiatomic or near-equiatomic composition, synthesized via mechanical alloying and spark plasma sintering, exhibiting high strength but potential susceptibility to embrittlement upon thermal exposure.
generation.intervention: Addition of 4.2 at% Cr to the base alloy prior to consolidation to induce the formation of a reticulated Laves phase network during sintering, rather than allowing uncontrolled precipitation of brittle intermetallics during thermal exposure.
generation.conditions: Thermal exposure at 1200–1400 °C for 100–1000 hours followed by quasi-static compressive loading at room temperature or elevated temperature (up to 0.6 Tm).
generation.structural_mediator: A continuous, reticulated network of Laves phase particles (e.g., Cr2Nb, (Fe,Cr)Nb) that forms preferentially at grain boundaries and triple junctions, acting as a barrier to crack propagation and stabilizing the grain boundary structure against excessive coarsening or brittle phase segregation.
generation.mechanism: The reticulated Laves phase network impedes the nucleation and growth of brittle intergranular cracks by pinning grain boundaries and distributing stress more uniformly, thereby preventing the catastrophic loss of toughness typically observed when single-phase BCC HEAs decompose into coarse, discontinuous brittle phases during prolonged thermal exposure. This mechanism leverages the synergistic effect of solid solution strengthening and the ductile-to-brittle transition mitigation provided by the Laves phase morphology.
generation.predicted_outcome: The Cr-modified alloy will exhibit a 15–25% higher fracture strain and 10–20% higher fracture toughness (measured via Charpy impact or compact tension tests) compared to the unmodified single-phase alloy after identical thermal exposure and loading, while maintaining comparable or slightly enhanced yield strength.
generation.baseline: The unmodified single-phase BCC HEA (e.g., NbMoTaWV or CrMoNbWV without Cr addition) subjected to the same thermal exposure and loading regime, which is expected to undergo phase decomposition into coarse, brittle intermetallics leading to significant embrittlement and reduced toughness.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis applies only to refractory BCC HEAs where Cr addition does not induce excessive formation of brittle oxides or carbides that would dominate the failure mechanism; it is valid for exposure temperatures below the melting point of the Laves phase but above the temperature where rapid grain coarsening occurs without phase stabilization.
generation.uncertainty: The exact volume fraction and morphology of the Laves phase required to optimize toughness without compromising strength are not fully defined; excessive Cr addition may lead to a continuous brittle network that reduces ductility, and the long-term stability of the Laves phase under cyclic thermal loading remains uncertain based on the provided evidence.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of refractory BCC HEA samples: (1) base alloy (no Cr) and (2) Cr-modified alloy (4.2 at% Cr). Subject both to thermal exposure at 1300 °C for 500 hours, then perform compressive testing and fracture toughness measurements (e.g., CTOD or J-integral). Use TEM and SEM to quantify Laves phase morphology and distribution.
measurements: Fracture strain and yield strength from compressive tests
Fracture toughness (K_IC or J_IC) from compact tension tests
Volume fraction and morphology of Laves phase via TEM/SEM
Grain size and phase distribution via EBSD
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if the Cr-modified alloy exhibits equal or lower fracture toughness and fracture strain compared to the unmodified alloy after thermal exposure, or if the Laves phase forms as a continuous brittle network rather than a reticulated structure, leading to premature intergranular failure.

cited_evidence.text: Abstract Concurrent strength–ductility improvement of HfMoTaTiZr is achieved via Cr addition and the underlying strengthening mechanism was discussed. 4.2 at% Cr addition into HfMoTaTiZr led to the formation of a Laves phase, in addition to the BCC phase. The hardness of HfMoTaTiZrCr 0.5 is 535.8 Hv 0.3 , 56.96% higher than the reference alloy HfMoTaTiZr. The yield strength and fracture strain of HfMoTaTiZrCr 0.5 reach 1750.6 ± 80.3 MPa and 14.0 ± 2.9%, respectively, 207.5 MPa and 20.6% higher than HfMoTaTiZr. Solid solution hardening and the presence of the intermetallic Laves phase are believed to be responsible for the enhancement in strength and the formation of a reticulated structure of the Laves phase in HfMoTaTiZrCr 0.5 results in the improvement in ductility.

In this study, bulk samples of a CrMoNbWV high-entropy alloy (HEA) were obtained for the first time by spark plasma sintering (SPS) of mechanically alloyed (MA) powders at 1200 °C, 1300 °C, and 1400 °C. Microstructure evolution, phase formation as well as wear and corrosion behavior were investigated. The MA powders’ phase composition was found to be represented by body-centered-cubic (BCC) solid solution. The solid solution partially decomposed to Laves phases under the sintering, such as Cr 2 Nb and (Fe, Cr)Nb, and NbVO 4 -VO oxides mixture. The temperature increase to 1400 °C led to a grain coarsening of the BCC phase and decreased the Laves phase content accompanied by precipitation at the grain boundaries. The sintered samples showed high hardness and compressive strength (2700–2800 MPa) at room temperature. The wear tests demonstrated excellent results in comparison to conventional wear-resistant composites. The obtained samples also exhibited high corrosion resistance under electrochemical tests in H 2 SO 4 solution. The CrMoNbWV HEA has comparable mechanical and corrosive properties with the WNbMoTaV type HEA, but at the same time has a reduced density: CrMoNbWV—10.55 g/cm
